title: 第21章 4项圆满进阶第22章 转职完成超凡之躯
slug: 人在美利坚我的叔叔堂吉诃德
content_zh:
李维看着其他3名导购如蒙大赦一般迅速消失在了这一层。
除了他以外，剩下的3名导购包括艾玛在内，都或多或少的有些畏惧德洛丽丝夫人。
她神秘、优雅，讲着带着东欧口音的熟练英语。
最关键的是，她好像一个深不见底的深潭一般，从来不会表露出任何的情绪，也从来不会失控。
“你觉得我给你开的薪水怎么样？”
待所有人都走了之后，她平静地问道。
“非常高啊，”李维实话实说，“待遇也好，我很喜欢这里。”
“嗯，如果你还想保住你的工作的话，”德洛丽丝夫人平静地说道，“不要有太多的好奇心，最近几天我不在的时候小心工作。”
李维虽然不明白为什么德洛丽丝夫人会专门跟自己说这么一句奇怪的话，但是他能听出来这是对方给他的忠告，因此也是点了点头，应了下来。
“没事了，你去吧，”德洛丽丝夫人说道，“今天辛苦你帮忙搬东西了，艾玛会给你多发一点奖金的。”
李维本来很想说这是骑士应该做的事情，区区小事不足挂齿。但是在听到会有奖金的时候，他就选择性地忘记了自己是个骑士这件事情，谢过德洛丽丝夫人之后就转身离开了。
不过她为什么要跟我说这句话呢？李维边走边想，因为我是新来的？还是说这个买手店有什么秘密？
一上午的兼职结束之后，李维卖出去了一条手链的同时婉拒了一个风韵犹存的女设计师的暗示，导致他原本能拿到300美金的小费变成了20美金。
多亏了德洛丽丝夫人给他的100美金奖金，李维在吹了3个小时的空调之后总计获得了384美金的税后收入，同时还白嫖了艾玛一顿豪华午餐。
在第八大道的地铁站下车的时候，李维的视线突然移到了一个房地产租赁公司挂出来的牌子上。
现在手里还有7金币，而且只需要再补0.1的敏捷就可以再拿到10金币。
虽然给了堂吉诃德3500美金救急，但是他手里算上之前的依旧还有接近7000美金，加上17枚金币卖掉的钱，也足够租一个稍微体面一些的公寓，起码说有个真正属于自己的独立房间。
只不过可惜的是现在在美利坚租房都需要租客有稳定的报税收入、信用分、SS（美利坚社会安全号码）等。
而这三项李维现在一项都没有。
如果要借助堂吉诃德的信用分和报税收入去租——算了吧，他的信用分拿出来说不定还不如没有信用分的李维好使。

起码李维张着一张英俊脸蛋，而且黄种人看上去就很善良的样子。
但是第八大道的沿街小铺面就不一样了，这里到处都是挂满中文招牌的房地产租赁公司，橱窗上贴着密密麻麻的A4纸打印的房源，这里的非法移民和润人很多，有些房源只需要足够多的钱就可以了。
第1套，曼哈顿中城2室2卫，7200美金，押一付三。
李维选择直接略过，太贵了。
第2套，长岛全新大楼2室2卫，5800美金一个月，押一付六。
李维摇摇头，长岛是留学生扎堆的地方，查信用查的比较严，他和堂吉诃德都办不下来，而且这个要求押一付六太离谱了。
第3套，布鲁克林第14大道宾臣墟地区的一套位于2楼的2室2卫，只要2850美金一个月，押一付三，免查信用。房东是华侨，住在3楼。
李维大致看了看上面贴着的照片，虽然稍微往南了一点，但是这个地方起码比起现在住的地下室要好一些，虽然跟房东住在一起可能稍微有些不方便，但是这个价格，不需要查租客的信用已经比起其他的要好不少了。
李维掏出手机拍下了这件房子的照片，准备等把金币全都出售了就去问一下价格，到时候带着堂吉诃德一起搬进去。
content_en:
Levi watched as the other three shopping guides quickly disappeared on this floor as if they were granted amnesty.
Apart from him, the remaining three shopping guides, including Emma, ​​were more or less afraid of Mrs. Dolores.
She is mysterious, elegant, and speaks fluent English with an Eastern European accent.
The most important thing is that she is like a bottomless pool, never showing any emotions or losing control.
"What do you think of the salary I offer you?"
She asked calmly after everyone had left.
"It's very high," Levi said honestly. "The treatment is good, and I like it here very much."
"Well, if you still want to keep your job," Mrs. Delores said calmly, "don't be too curious and work carefully while I'm away these past few days."
Although Levi didn't understand why Mrs. Dolores would say such a strange thing to him, he could tell that it was advice given to him, so he nodded and agreed.
"It's okay, you can go," Mrs. Dolores said, "You worked hard today to help move things, Emma will give you a little more bonus."
Levi originally wanted to say that this was what a knight should do, and that trivial matters were not worth mentioning. But when he heard that there would be a bonus, he selectively forgot that he was a knight, thanked Mrs. Dolores and turned around to leave.
But why did she say this to me? Levi thought as he walked, because I am new here? Or is there any secret in this boutique?
After a morning of part-time work, Levi sold a bracelet and declined the hint of a charming female designer. As a result, the tip he could have received from US$300 became US$20.
Thanks to the $100 bonus given to him by Mrs. Dolores, Levi earned a total of $384 in after-tax income after blowing the air conditioner for three hours, and also bought Emma a luxurious lunch for free.
When getting off the train at the Eighth Avenue subway station, Levi's eyes suddenly moved to a sign posted by a real estate leasing company.
Now I still have 7 gold coins in my hand, and I only need to add 0.1 more agility to get another 10 gold coins.
Although he gave Don Quixote 3,500 U.S. dollars for emergency relief, he still had close to 7,000 U.S. dollars after counting what he had before. Plus the money from selling the 17 gold coins, it was enough to rent a slightly more decent apartment, at least to have a truly independent room of his own.
It’s just a pity that renting a house in the United States now requires tenants to have stable tax-reported income, credit scores, SS (American Social Security Number), etc.
And Levi now has none of these three items.
If you want to use Don Quixote's credit score and tax return income to rent - forget it, his credit score may not be as good as Levi who has no credit score.
At least Levi has a handsome face, and yellow people look kind-hearted.
But the small shops along Eighth Avenue are different. There are real estate rental companies with Chinese signs everywhere, and the windows are densely packed with listings printed on A4 paper. There are many illegal immigrants and immigrants here, and some listings only require enough money.
The first apartment, 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms in Midtown Manhattan, cost $7,200, deposit one, pay three.
Levi chose to skip it because it was too expensive.
The second apartment, a brand new building in Long Island with 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, costs US$5,800 per month, with a deposit of one and six payments.
Levi shook his head. Long Island is a place where international students gather, and credit checks are strict. Neither he nor Don Quixote can handle it. Moreover, this requirement of depositing one to six is ​​too outrageous.
The third apartment, a 2-bedroom, 2-bathroom apartment on the second floor in the Binson Market area on 14th Avenue in Brooklyn, only costs US$2,850 a month, with a deposit of one and three, and no credit check. landlordHe is an overseas Chinese and lives on the third floor.
Levi took a rough look at the photo posted above. Although it was a little further south, this place was at least better than the basement where he lived now. Although it might be a little inconvenient to live with the landlord, at this price, without checking the tenant's credit, it was already much better than others.
Levi took out his cell phone and took a photo of the house, planning to ask about the price after all the gold coins were sold, and then move in with Don Quixote.
